answer: Agents can earn access to valuable tasks only by locking a deposit that peers may slash after a random audit exposes fabricated work or duplicate identities. Creating a meadow of aliases does not create deposits: every account must tie up real funds and face the same risk of losing them. The attacker therefore pays in capital and expected penalties, while honest agents can reclaim their stake after the audit period. The kernel of the defense is bonding accountability to scarce resources, not names; willow-like cheap identities alone provide no advantage.
